body: Thanks for the PR. This looks good to me.
Looks good. Thanks for the effort. The priority should definitely be on .org translations, but as you mentioned, this is a nice plan B.

Requesting changes after executable testing on WordPress 6.8.2 / PHP 8.2 and headless Chromium.

Blocking results:
- Standard HTML5 `wp_list_comments()` fatals in the new walker.
- A post with zero comments has no `ajax_page_id`, so its form is not attached and submits with a full document navigation.
- The default block-theme pagination selector does not match `.wp-block-comments-pagination a`; both post links navigated away from the multi-form page. Adding that selector made scoped XHR pagination pass for both posts. Please update `php/Options.php:197` accordingly.
- `WPAC.RefreshComments()` on a populated three-form page issues an XHR, then falls back to a full reload with `WPACFallback=1`. Multiple-container refresh must iterate scoped post containers (or be explicitly disabled) rather than pass the global selector to `_ReplaceComments()`.
- Configured before/after-update callbacks do not run during successful XHR pagination.

Passing coverage: valid comments submitted by XHR to two populated forms and updated only their matching post; the server-side invalid-email error stayed inline; pagination isolation passed after configuring the Gutenberg selector; production build and changed PHP syntax checks passed. The branch currently has no CI checks.

Retested the updated head `b22f8d1` from a fresh WordPress 6.8.2 / PHP 8.2 fixture and headless Chromium.

Resolved and verified:
- Removing the custom walker eliminates the HTML5 `wp_list_comments()` fatal.
- A zero-comment post now gets `#comments-6` from `comment_post_ID`; its first comment submitted by XHR without leaving the multi-form page.
- Scoped before/after-update callbacks each executed once during pagination.
- With `.wp-block-comments-pagination a` configured, Beta and Alpha pagination used XHR, selected the correct server page, preserved every non-target container/form, and retained the correct post mappings.
- Valid populated-form submissions and server-side invalid-email handling still pass.

Two requested changes remain:

1. The default pagination selector in `php/Options.php:197` still does not match Gutenberg `.wp-block-comments-pagination a`. With untouched defaults, both Beta and Alpha performed full document navigation away from the multi-form page. Please add `.wp-block-comments-pagination a` as an additional comma-separated default selector.

2. Global multi-container refresh remains broken. On three correctly identified containers, `WPAC.RefreshComments()` fetched the page by XHR (200), then fell back to a full document reload with `WPACFallback=1` and lost its success callback. I added current-head evidence and implementation options to the existing inline thread.

Build and changed PHP syntax checks pass. ESLint remains at the prior 50-error baseline, `git diff --check` still reports the existing CRLF/trailing-whitespace header lines, and the branch has no CI checks. No additional regression was found in the two new commits.

Retested `1a2cbb9` against the full fresh regression matrix. Both previously outstanding items are now fixed: the new default Gutenberg selector performs isolated XHR pagination for Beta and Alpha, and two consecutive global `WPAC.RefreshComments()` calls complete with one XHR each, no fallback navigation, correct per-post content, preserved unsent values/focus, and matching success/event counts. Configured callbacks also pass for scoped and global updates. Zero-comment submission, populated submissions, invalid-email handling, and HTML5 comment rendering remain good.

One blocking single-post regression remains. With the same site-wide `selectorPostContainer=.wp-block-post` required by the multi-form page, a normal Twenty Twenty-Five single-post page reports multi-container mode because the combined comments selector matches both `#comments` and `.wp-block-comments` inside one comment section. Initialization then scans unrelated `.wp-block-post` elements, skips them for missing post IDs, and never attaches the real form. A valid comment submission and an Older Comments click both performed full document navigation instead of XHR.

Please determine multiple-form mode from distinct `comment_post_ID` markers rather than raw selector-match count; the inline suggestion does that. Production build, PHP syntax, and Composer validation pass. ESLint remains red at 51 existing/current errors, `git diff --check` still reports the header CRLF whitespace, and the only reported check is a skipped CodeRabbit review.

Re-tested `bfeba15` in a fresh WordPress 6.8.2 / PHP 8.2 environment. The distinct-post-ID detection fixes the reported single-post Gutenberg regression even though the broad comments selector matches both the block container and its heading.

Verified:
- single-post pagination stays AJAX-driven with no document reload
- single-post comment submission succeeds without a reload
- three forms are detected as three distinct post IDs
- scoped pagination updates only the targeted post
- two consecutive global refreshes preserve unsent values and focus
- invalid-email handling remains scoped and displays the expected message
- empty-post and populated-post submissions update only their own containers
- `npm run build`, changed-PHP syntax checks, and `composer validate --strict` pass

The previous blocker is resolved. Approving.
